hints: Read Felix's and Teddy's statements side by side. Can both of them be true, or both of them false?
That is the opposites shortcut: exactly one of Felix and Teddy is telling the truth. The rule needs three true statements in all.
So Marta's and Sam's statements must both be true. Sam's clears Sam, and Marta's clears Marta and Teddy, which leaves Felix.

solution.key_idea: Felix and Teddy contradict each other, so only one of them is truthful, and the other two true statements must be Marta's and Sam's.
steps: Felix says Marta didn't take the postcards, and Teddy says she did. They are opposites, so exactly one of them is telling the truth.
The rule needs three true statements, so the other two, Marta's and Sam's, must both be true.
Sam's statement clears Sam. Marta's statement clears Marta and Teddy. That leaves Felix.
Check Felix: Felix's, Marta's and Sam's statements are true, and only Teddy's is false. That is exactly three, so Felix fits.
Test Teddy, Marta or Sam instead, and each one gives only two true statements.
solution.epilogue: Felix had scooped up the whole stack, sure they were free, to hand out with every rowboat rental. He brought the stack back, bought fifty for his rental customers, and called the deal shipshape.
